subject: Designing a cost & packaging split for retention, tracing and dashboards
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@cloudhaven.com>, Mark Patel <mark.patel@cloudhaven.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Designing a cost & packaging split for retention, tracing and dashboards

Hi Sarah / Mark —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we talked about, the three add-ons (retention, distributed tracing, and the advanced dashboards pack) are the main drivers of variability on your bill. To make the next step easier for your procurement team I want to propose two pragmatic packaging paths so you can evaluate economics vs. coverage quickly.

Quick ask: can you confirm the following usage mix for Feb so we can size the tiers accurately?
- Avg daily retention volume (GB/day): ~700 GB/day
- Peak ingested trace spans/day: ~12M spans
- Concurrent dashboard seats for power users: ~8

If those numbers are off please correct. Based on our benchmarks I can outline: (A) a conservative retention slab with surge cushion + flat tracing slab, or (B) a commit-based blended price with a higher discount but a minimum commit. I’ll include recommended concession paths we can use in negotiation.

I’ve attached a short pricing canvas we use to map scenarios — will send the SOW draft once you confirm the mix.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: cloudhaven-usage-canvas.xlsx (stub)
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@cloudhaven.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Patel <mark.patel@cloudhaven.com>, procurement@cloudhaven.com
Date: Wed, 01 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Designing a cost & packaging split for retention, tracing and dashboards

Hi Ben —

Thanks — that aligns closely with our internal metrics for Feb. A couple of clarifications:
- Retention: the 700 GB/day estimate is correct, but we retain for 90 days for most events and 365 for a small subset (audit logs).
- Tracing: 12M spans/day is the aggregate; peak per-region is ~5.5M.
- Dashboards: 8 power seats, ~25 casual seats (read-only).

Procurement wants to see: 1) a committed discount path (12 months) vs pay-as-you-go, and 2) an explicit surcharge or smoothing approach for surge days. Also, any seat-based vs usage-based tradeoffs for dashboards would be helpful — our PMs care about predictability for forecasting.

Can you include the two scenarios you mentioned (conservative slab + commit blended) and a recommended starting discount range? We’ll route the SOW to procurement after we see numbers.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudHaven
sarah.lin@cloudhaven.com

Kim / Michael —

Fwding CloudHaven’s reply (below). They want two clear commercial options and guidance on how to smooth surge days (surcharge vs. buffer slabs). Procurement will want a starter discount range to expect.

Please propose:
- Option A: PAYG slabs (retention tiers, trace per-M span slab, dashboard seats) with surge smoothing rules and a conservative price.
- Option B: 12-month commit (GB-month + spans-month + seat commitment) with a blended discount (tiered by commit band) and a smaller surge surcharge.

Include recommended list prices (per GB-month, per million spans, per dashboard seat/month), suggested discount bands by commit ($100k, $250k, $500k ARR), and a sample invoice month to show delta vs PAYG. They asked for predictability so add an example smoothing rule (e.g., 3x daily buffer before surcharge, monthly true-up).

I’ve pasted Sarah’s note below. Help prioritize the commit thresholds — CloudHaven is mid-market but rapidly growing, so be conservative on minimums.

Thanks —
Ben

Subject: RE: CloudHaven pricing ask — proposed commercial scenarios

Ben / Michael —

Thanks — I sketched two market-aligned scenarios and a concession path. High level: both are anchored to three unit prices (GB-month, per-1M spans, dashboard seat/month). I’m including the quick numbers here so you can share a concise version with the customer; full line-item pricing + example month is in the attached PDF (cloudhaven-maP_pricing_v1.pdf).

Option A — PAYG slabs (conservative):
- Retention: $0.045 per GB-month in base tier up to 1TB/day effective, with step-down tiers beyond.
- Tracing: $14 per 1M spans (ingested), slabbed monthly.
- Dashboards: $55 / power seat / month, $10 / casual seat / month.
- Surge smoothing: monthly true-up + 5% monthly buffer before surcharge; surcharge = 1.25x list on overage.

Option B — 12-month commit (blended):
- Anchor list: $0.035 per GB-month; $11 per 1M spans; $45 / power seat / month (casual unchanged).
- Commit bands (annual ARR): $100k -> 10% discount off anchor, $250k -> 18%, $500k+ -> 26% (applies to blended components).
- Surge smoothing: 10% committed buffer included; overage billed at 1.10x list with monthly true-up.

Recommended concession path:
- If procurement asks for deeper discount, use seat-bundling (add 6 months free for casual seats) as a non-recurring concession before touching unit price.
- Approve a one-time onboarding credit (up to $15k) to close faster.

I attached the SOW skeleton so we can forward after Ben confirms numbers with CloudHaven.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Follow-up: two pricing paths for retention, tracing & dashboards (attached)

Hi Sarah / Mark —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Per your ask, attached are two concise commercial paths and a short SOW draft: the PAYG slab option (Option A) and the 12-month commit blended option (Option B). I’ve pulled the key numbers from our commercial team below so you can share with procurement quickly.

Summary (high level):
- Option A (PAYG slabs): conservative list pricing, best for bursty workloads. Surge smoothing: 5% monthly buffer then 1.25x overage.
- Option B (12-month commit): lower unit prices across retention and tracing, includes 10% buffer and a smaller overage multiplier; discount bands scale with ARR commit (10/18/26%).

Suggested next steps:
1) Review attached PDF + SOW with procurement.
2) Let me know which option you prefer; if Option B, confirm an ARR band to lock in the pricing.
3) If procurement needs deeper commercial flexibility we can offer a seat-bundling concession or a one-time onboarding credit (up to $15k) in lieu of price cuts.

I’ve attached the full line-item PDF and a draft SOW for signature. Happy to walk procurement through the sample invoice and smoothing rules — we can do a 30-minute call early next week.

Best,
